method: Azure-proposed narrow corrections inspected by Codex before application; acceptance requires a fresh separate review.

patches.old:
After I had passed the beast and gone forward about thirty feet, a virgin met me, adorned as though coming from a bridal chamber. She was dressed entirely in white, with white sandals, and veiled to her forehead. Her covering was bound with a headband, and her hair was white.[a]

2. From the earlier visions I recognized that she was the church, and I became more cheerful. She greeted me, saying, “Greetings, man!” I greeted her in return: “Greetings, lady!”

3. She asked me, “Did nothing meet you?” I said to her, “Lady, an enormous beast, capable of destroying whole peoples! But through the Lord’s power and abundant mercy I escaped it.”

4. “You escaped safely,” she said, “because you cast your care upon God and opened your heart toward the Lord, believing that you could be saved through nothing except the great and glorious name.[b] For this reason the Lord sent his angel who oversees the beasts, whose name is Thegri, and shut its mouth so that it would not harm you.[c] You have escaped great affliction through your faith and because you did not waver when you saw such an enormous beast.”

5. “Go, then, and tell the Lord’s chosen ones about his mighty deeds. Tell them that this beast is a sign of the great affliction to come. If you prepare yourselves and repent toward the Lord with your whole heart, you will be able to escape it, if your heart becomes pure and without blemish and you serve the Lord blamelessly for the remaining days of your life. Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he himself will set them right.”[d]

6. “Trust in the Lord, you who waver, because he can do all things. He turns his anger away from you and sends scourges upon you who waver.[e] Woe to those who heard these words and disobeyed! It would have been better for them not to have been born.”

patches.reason: Reconsideration of the prior lexical rendering of μίτρα: ἐν μίτρᾳ δὲ ἦν ἡ κατακάλυψις αὐτῆς describes the covering in relation to a mitra, without a verb of binding or fastening. Propose the general covering term “head-wrap” rather than asserting a separate fastening mechanism; the accompanying note preserves the construction and lexical alternatives.

patches.old: White hair follows the working 1891 text and Athos, Lake (1907), Plate IV line 28. Primary Sinaiticus project XML, chapter23.1 word42, has chiras, “hands,” with an adjacent verb corrected to “had” by S1. Alternative: “She had white hands.” The project marks a letter of the earlier verb uncertain; no fresh manuscript photograph collation is claimed. “Headband” renders mitra; “turban” is an alternative covering term, retained in the archived reader history.
